stem:
Variations in the length of day and night time from season to season are due to –
1. The earth’s rotation on its axis
2. The earth’s revolution around the sun in an elliptical manner.
3. Latitudinal position of the place.
4. Revolution of the earth on axis
Which of the above-mentioned statement/statements is/are correct?
expl: Earth is tilted on its axis. If Earth had not been tilted on its axis, then days and nights would have been equal everywhere. In the same way, if Earth had not been revolving around the sun, then there would always have been longer days and shorter nights in one hemisphere and longer nights and shorter days in the other hemisphere. But except the equatorial line, the difference in the length of days and nights is seen in different seasons. On the equatorial line, days and nights are always equal.

(2) Variation in altitude between continents and oceans

(4) Heavy rains in the interior as compared to coasts.

expl: The reason behind the high annual range of temperature in the interior of the continents is the thermal difference between land and water. The land gets heated rapidly through the insolation of the sun whereas water gets heated very slowly. Due to this, the weather of the coastal areas remains cold compared to the terrestrial regions. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. However the other statements given in the codes are not true.

expl: The Mediterranean climate has been developed between 300- 400 latitudes in both hemispheres. The Mediterranean type of climate is characterized by dry summers and wet winters. The basic cause of this type of climate is the shifting of pressure and wind belts. In summer, when Sun is overhead at Tropic of Cancer, the Westerlies belt is shifted poleward. The prevailing Trade winds are off-shore (terrestrial) and there is 'no rain'. The Mediterranean lands receive most of their precipitation in winter when the westerlies shift equatorward. The westerlies are associated with temperate cyclones and blow from sea surfaces, hence being moist yields sufficient rainfall in coastal areas.

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to-Mediterranean climate:
1. It receives rainfall in winter season.
2. Due to winter solstice, air pressure belts shift to the South.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
expl: The Mediterranean climate generally develops between 300 and 400 Latitudes in both hemispheres, primarily on the western sides of continents. A key characteristic of the Mediterranean climate is that rainfall occurs in winter, while summers are usually dry. The development of the Mediterranean climate occurs due to the shifting of pressure and wind belts caused by the northward and southward movement of the sun (Uttarayan and Dakshinayan) During winter (in the Northern Hemisphere), at the time of the winter solstice when sun is over the Tropic of Capricon, the westerly winds originating over the ocean expand into these northern latitudes. Since these mositure wind are associated with temperate cyclones, they cause rainfall. During winter (in the contexst of the Southern Hemisphere), at the time of the summer solstice when the sun is over the tropic of cancer, the expansion of westerly winds originating over the oceans into these latitude bring winter rainfall. Note : Statement (2) is technically incorrect. It is only valid for the mediterranean climate in the Northern Hemisphere. The development of the mediterranean climate is not solely due to the southward shift of pressure belts during the winter solstice but also due to the northward shift to Pressure belts during the summer solstice (which corresponds to winter in the southern Hemisphere).

expl: The Western European type climate (Climate of Western Europe) is found between 400 and 650 latitudes along the western edges of continents within the westerlies belt. This climate is humid, with rainfall occurring throughout the year in all seasons. However, winter generally receives slightly more rainfall than summer. There is variation in the amount of rainfall from one place to another. Generally, the amount of rainfall decreases as one moves from the coast towards the interior regions. Note : The climate of Western Europe is here taken to mean the Western European type climate. However, Mediterranean climate conditions prevail in the southern part of Western Europe. The main areas are: Northwestern Europe, west coast of North America, north of California, southern Chile, southeastern Australia and New Zealand. Due to marine influence, the temperature is moderate and in winter, it is warmer than for its latitude. Generally, the mean temperature in summer months ranges from 15°-20°C and in winter it ranges from 4° to 10°C. The annual and daily ranges of temperature are small or low. Precipitation occurs throughout the year. Precipitation varies greatly from 50 to 250 cm.

With reference to the “EL-NINO”, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
(1) El Nino involves appearance of warm current off the coast of Peru in eastern pacific.
(2) This warm current increase the temperature of water on the Peruvian coast by 10°C there by increasing the amount of Plankton in the sea.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-Code :
expl: EI-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to seven years, bringing drought, floods and other weather extremes to different parts of the world. The system involves oceanic and atmospheric phenomena with the appearance of warm currents off the coast of Peru in the eastern Pacific and affects weather in many places including India. EI-Nino is merely an extension of the warm equatorial current which gets replaced temporarily by cold Peruvian current or Humbold current. This current increases the temperature of water on the Peruvian coast by 10°C. This results in: (i) the distortion of equatorial atmospheric circulation; (ii) irregularities in the evaporation of sea water; (iii) reduction in the amount of Planktons which further reduces the number of fish in the sea. Hence option(a) is the correct answer.

expl: El Nino and La Nina are weather patterns. El Nino is associated with an increase in the temperature of the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean water, while La Nina is related to the cooling of the western Pacific Ocean water. During La Nina, trade winds become stronger than usual, pushing more warm water toward Asia. Therefore, El Nino and La Nina are not storms. During El Nino, the process of upwelling in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean slows down or stops, leading to a decrease in phytoplankton off the coast.

stem: 'Vegetation is the true index of climate'. This statement is associated with :
expl: German-Russian botanist and climatologist Vladimir Koppen presented a descriptive classification of the world's climate in the year 1884, which was revised and refined in the years 1918, 1931 and 1936. Koppen has considered vegetation as the true indicator of climate. This has made the five vegetation zones of the world proposed by Candoll in 1874 AD the basis of the division of the world's climate. Later, like Koppen, Thornthwaite also propounded that vegetation is an indicator of climate and that the amount of rainfall and temperature has a substantial effect on vegetation, but he took evaporation into account. On this basis, Thornthwaite has given importance to precipitation effectiveness in demarcation of climate. Thornthwaite has accepted vegetation as an indirect element of climate.
